subject: Adding additonal copy number algorithms in aroma.affymetrix

messages.author: 6a5f89dafa3973ea
messages.subject: Adding additonal copy number algorithms in aroma.affymetrix
parts:
Dear Dr. H Bengtsson,

I recently discovered the aroma.affymetrix package, I really like the
method and I'm
very interested in using it to do the preprocessing before applying my
copy
number segmentation algorithm:
http://bioinformatics.oxfordjournals.org/cgi/content/short/24/3/309

I also plan to evaluate it on the entire 270 Hapmap Affy6.0 reference
samples.
I already did a test run with the example you provide using CBS on the
google group.

I already have some experience in using CBS so I would really
appreciate
if you could tell me which would be the functions that I should modify
in
aroma.affymetrix so I can replace the CBS by my algorithm.
I would really appreciate your help.

Best regards,

> very interested in using it to do the preprocessing before applying my

> number segmentation algorithm:

>
> I also plan to evaluate it on the entire 270 Hapmap Affy6.0 reference
> samples.
> I already did a test run with the example you provide using CBS on the
> google group.
>
> I already have some experience in using CBS so I would really
> appreciate
> if you could tell me which would be the functions that I should modify
> in
> aroma.affymetrix so I can replace the CBS by my algorithm.
> I would really appreciate your help.

Great that you consider adding a class for your GADA method. You need
to create a subclass GadaModel of the abstract class
CopyNumberSegmentationModel. This is as easy as:

setConstructorS3("GadaModel", function(...) {
extend(CopyNumberSegmentationModel(...), "GadaModel")
})

Then you need to provide a method getAsteriskTags() that returns the
tag(s) replacing any tag "*":

setMethodS3("getAsteriskTags", "GadaModel", function(this, collapse=NULL, ...) {
tags <- "GADA";
if (isPaired(this))
tags <- c(tags, "paired");
tags <- paste(tags, collapse=collapse);
tags;
}, protected=TRUE)

Already now you can try the following, assuming you have a
CnChipEffectSet object named 'ces' :

> gada <- GadaModel(ces);
> print(gada);
> print(getPath(gada));

Note how the "root" path of your GadaModel starts with 'gadaData/'.
That is the output path where (you will) store you model
estimates/results. Download the source of aroma.affymetrix and you
will see how this is done for CbsModel in source file R/CbsModel.R.

You can now even try the following:

> fit(gada, arrays=1:2, chromosomes=22, verbose=-20);

You'll see it that the framework will load the chip effects for the
chromosomes of interest, calculate the raw CN (log2 ratios) and try to
call fitOne() on your GadaModel object. As you see you will get an
error because you still haven't define fitOne() for the GadaModel
class. This is the method that will take the data and do the fitting
etc and return the results.

fitOne() should take an argument 'data' which is a Jx6 matrix where
the number of rows J is the number of loci, and the six columns are x,
M, sdTheta, sdM, chipType, and unit. To understand what this object
is, try:

> files <- getMatrixChipEffectFiles(gada, array=1);
> ceList <- files[,"test"];
> refList <- files[,"reference"];
> data <- getRawCnData(gada, ceList=ceList, refList=refList, chromosome=22, verbose=-10);
> str(data)
num [1:74, 1:6] 15685581 16604328 16958128 17506879 18008688 ...
- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
..$ : NULL
..$ : chr [1:6] "x" "M" "sdTheta" "sdM" ...
> plot(data[,c("x","M")], ylim=c(-3,3))

So, 'x' is the genomic position, 'M' is the log2 ratio. These are
probably the only ones you will need. [The 'sdM' ('sdTheta') is the
estimated standard of each M (theta), and 'chiptype' and 'unit' is the
chip type and the CDF unit index for the particular locus. The 'chip
type' is useful if data from two or more chip type are to be
segmented.]

Assume you have an R function fitGada(x,M) that takes positions 'x'
and log-ratios 'M' and identifies CN regions returned in some
structure. For simplicity, assume the return structure is of class
"GadaFit". Then your fitOne() should look something like (excluding
any 'verbose' statements):

setMethodS3("fitOne", "GadaModel", function(this, data, ..., verbose=FALSE) {
fit <- fitGada(x=data[,"x"], M=data[,"M"]);
# In case your fitGada() does not return an object with class, then do
# class(fit) <- "GadaFit"
# In case your fitGada() does not return the raw CNs, add them here
# fit$data <- data;
fit;
}, private=TRUE) # fitOne()

You probably want to add verbose output etc. See how this is done for
the CbsModel (see R/CbsModel.fitOne.R). You can also look how it is
done for the GladModel.

You next have to write a extractRawCopyNumbers() for "GadaFit" that
returns a RawCopyNumber object, e.g.

setMethodS3("extractRawCopyNumbers", "GadaFit", functionfunction (fit, ...) {
data <- fitt$data;
RawCopyNumbers(cn=data[,"M"], x=data[,"x"])
})

and extractCopyNumberRegions() for "GadaFit" that returns a
CopyNumberRegions object, e.g.

setMethodS3("extractCopyNumberRegions", "GadaFit", function (fit, ...) {
CopyNumberRegions(chromosome=fit[,"chr"], start=fit[,"start"],
stop=fit[,"stop"],
mean=fit[,"meanLevel"], count=fit[,"nbrOfLoci"]);
})

That should be it (but I might have forgot something). Hope this get
you started. So look at CbsModel/GladModel and what methods are
called in fit() of the CopyNumberSegmentationModel class. Turn on
maximum verbose output, e.g. verbose=-50 when you call fit() to see
what data is passed and where you get errors etc.

I'll be happy to add the your segmentation class aroma.affymetrix when
you get it up and running.

Cheers

Henrik

>
> Best regards,
> >
